bullets.title: AI bubble fears intensify: Korean neocloud IPO crash, hedge fund de-risking, bearish signals across semis
bullets.body: Elice, a Korean neocloud provider, plunged 32% on its IPO debut — worst on record for a $100M+ Korean listing — despite a 400x oversubscribed retail tranche, triggering broad AI-sector selloffs (Kospi -3.7%, SOXL -67% from June peak). Hedge funds reduced net equity exposure to the 30th percentile following -3.1 std dev selling in AI winners, and 80% of 35 stocks in Hedgeye's AI 'Big Theme' deck now signal bearish TREND. CDS volumes surged on AI unwind hedges, and SoftBank CDS hit a four-year high.

bullets.title: Pre-market tape: S&P +0.25%, 10Y yield +3bps to 5.11%, WTI +2.3% to $100.79; semis -2%
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures +19.3pts (+0.25%) to 7715 as of pre-market, but Nasdaq futures -0.5% with the semiconductor index (SOXX) down 2%. The 10-year yield extended to 5.11% (+3bps), and WTI crude surged 2.28% to $100.79 on Middle East geopolitical escalation (RAF Typhoons to Saudi Arabia, two tankers struck in Strait of Hormuz). Crypto/neocloud names fell 4-5% on Elice contagion.

bullets.title: Oil spike: WTI surges to ~$100-107 range on Hegseth-Netanyahu meeting and Strait of Hormuz tanker strikes
bullets.body: WTI rose 2.3-4.2% to $100.79-$107.50 depending on source, driven by geopolitical tensions including Iran-U.S. talks breakdown, RAF Typhoon deployment to defend Saudi Arabia, and two oil tankers struck by mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Energy stocks showing bullish trend signals even as broader equities weaken.

bullets.title: AI capex prisoner's dilemma: hyperscalers cash-flow negative; neocloud financing stress rising
bullets.body: AWS CFO noted that ~$5B/month in NVDA GB300 deliveries has taken the company free cash flow negative. Anthropic is offering Blackstone >10% yield on $60B chip financing (Project North Star) vs. 8.5% on a prior deal, signaling investor caution. Neoclouds fund 70% of capex via contract-backed SPV debt but face rising cost of capital as unsecured/convertible markets tighten; CRWV carries ~$51B in debt and lease obligations.

bullets.title: NVDA: Rubin mass production delayed to Q2 2027; China orders 6M+ cards but export controls limit fill to 5-10%
bullets.body: Hedgeye removes NVDA long on Rubin delay pushed to Q2 2027 from expected Q4 2026/Q1 2027, with neocloud financing stress threatening to temper system purchases. ByteDance, Alibaba, and Tencent placed ~$35B in NVDA RTX PRO 5500 orders, but NVDA can only fulfill 5-10% of 6M+ unit demand due to US export controls. NVDA GPU pricing remains stable but non-renewals/cancellations from neoclouds are expected to increase.

bullets.title: Market regime: Value outperforming Momentum; 22V recommends Value-Momentum blend as AI uncertainty dominates
bullets.body: 22V's Macro Regime Model sits in Normal Economic Expansion but Market Internal Regime has returned to Risk Averse, dominant since the June Momentum selloff. Financial conditions tightening in 2H26 reinforces risk-off internals; Realized Value, Comparative Value, and Cash Return have outperformed since early October. BAA-AAA spreads remain unusually tight, but 22V is avoiding long Momentum exposure because AI buildout ROI uncertainty outweighs expansion tailwinds.

bullets.title: JPM tactically bullish despite selloff: favors Cyclicals, selective Tech/Semis dips, large-cap Banks
bullets.body: JPM retains a tactical bullish stance: ASML/TSMC posted healthy earnings and consumer data remains resilient, with 75% of IMF survey respondents expecting S&P >7,500 by end-2027. Key support for SPX at 7,616-7,643 then 7,507; SOX at critical inflection with break below 10,445-10,895 risking acceleration lower. META earnings and NVDA's GTC Berlin are flagged as the key tests of AI revenue delivery.

bullets.title: 10-year yield at 5.11%: France fiscal crisis adds European sovereign stress; OAT-Bund spread at 2012 levels
bullets.body: France's government debt is approaching 120% of GDP with OAT-Bund spreads widening to levels last seen during the 2012 European debt crisis; French 10-year yields now exceed Greek yields. The correlation between French and US 10-year yields has fallen from 90% in August to 40% in October, suggesting moderated US spillover risk. German October ZEW Economic Sentiment fell to 28.1 vs. 32.0 consensus, and UK jobless claims rose more than expected.

bullets.title: Fed recognizes AI capex as inflationary; rate hikes risk hitting smaller firms harder
bullets.body: The Fed has formally acknowledged the AI investment boom as an inflationary force, but markets are flagging that rate hikes to address AI-driven inflation would disproportionately hit smaller firms and households. Structural elevation in borrowing costs is expected, with mortgage rates near 7.5% pressuring housing; GS forecasts existing home sales of 3.9M and single-family starts of 0.87M for 2027.

bullets.title: AI earnings growth decelerating: from ~100% in 2026 to ~30% in 2027 and ~22% in 2028
bullets.body: Jefferies quant strategy warns that AI earnings growth will decelerate sharply — from ~100% this year to 30% in 2027 and 22% in 2028 — as high capex intensity, longer cash-flow lead times, and tighter funding conditions raise execution risk. Outside AI, earnings revisions remain low but are turning steadily positive, making ex-AI areas increasingly attractive alternatives for positioning.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples compressing: All-Security index -13% WoW; IGV -1.3% YTD vs S&P +12.8%
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.7x FY+2 EV/Sales and All-Security at 8.5x, with SaaS multiples down 7.9% WoW and security multiples down 13.3% WoW amid broad tech de-risking. IGV has returned -1.3% YTD vs. S&P 500 +12.8%, with software holding better than semis on a relative basis (IGV still bullish trend per Hedgeye).

bullets.title: Key earnings this week: NFLX tonight, META tomorrow, TXN/SPOT/WDC/STX later in week
bullets.body: NFLX reports after close today (consensus EPS $0.82, revenue $12.87B) amid reports of slipping US engagement and executive departures; META reports Tuesday AH (EPS $6.60, revenue $63.34B) with 2027 capex guidance ($190-200B expected) as the critical print for the AI infrastructure narrative. WDC and STX report Wednesday AH (EPS $4.09/$7.41 respectively), with HDD fundamentals a key read on AI storage demand.

bullets.title: Memory prices rising: Q4 NAND +30% QoQ, DRAM +20% QoQ; Taiwan September export orders beat on AI chips
bullets.body: Q4 NAND prices are expected up 30% QoQ and DRAM up 20% QoQ on AI inference demand, even as OpenRouter token consumption declined 4.65% WoW and the Silicon Token Expenditure Index remains soft. Taiwan September export orders exceeded expectations at $114B driven by AI chip demand; B200/H100 rental pricing is on an uptrend with demand still exceeding supply on older chips.

bullets.title: Danny Moses: megacap tech preferred over speculative AI; CRWV and NVDA face structural risks
bullets.body: Moses draws a direct parallel between current AI infrastructure spending and the late-1990s fiber-optic boom, preferring GOOGL, AMZN, META, and MSFT on pullbacks for their underlying business flexibility over speculative plays. NVDA faces GPU pricing pressure and a concentrated customer base (~70% of receivables from five accounts); CRWV carries ~$51B in debt and lease obligations with uncertain profitability. AI sector concentration in OpenAI and Anthropic mirrors pre-2008 securitization risk.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce wave emerging: Google Universal Cart live; Shopify key beneficiary; large retailers advantaged
bullets.body: Google has deployed its Universal Cart across the US with early partners including Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta, Walmart, and Shopify merchants. Personal AI agents currently favor only the top 1-2 dozen large trusted retailers; Instinct is approaching $1B in annualized transaction volume. Shopify is positioned as the long-term beneficiary if agentic shopping accelerates, with sponsored ads evolving toward conversational API-based formats.

bullets.title: Datacenter capex growing 30%+ annually through 2029; EQIX/DLR favored on NIMBY dynamics and JV structures
bullets.body: AI datacenter capex is forecast to grow 30%+ annually 2026-2029 vs. 10-20% historically, with datacenter opposition rising from 42% to 75% YoY but spending still at a record $75B+ annual pace. 30GW of 2028-2030 forecast capacity sits in TX, GA, and OH with midterm election risk; DLR and EQIX benefit from decades of local community relationships and JV funding structures. Multiple sell-side desks flag EQIX/DLR street estimates as too low with hockey-stick growth ahead.

bullets.title: Holiday sales: NRF forecasts +4.2% Y/Y growth to ~$1T; consumer caution persists from rates and inflation
bullets.body: NRF forecasts 2026 holiday sales growth of 4.2% Y/Y to ~$1T (Bain: 4.5%, Deloitte: 4.4%), above 2025's 3.1% actual but below some expectations. Retailers are hiring 325K-375K seasonal workers in-line with 2025, amid consumer caution from elevated gas prices, sticky inflation, high rates (~7.5% mortgage), and elevated debt levels — reflecting a K-shaped economy pressuring lower-income households.

bullets.title: Macau GGR -5% YoY in October MTD, tracking well below consensus; downgrades likely
bullets.body: Macau GGR for the first 19 days of October averaged MOP742M/day, tracking 5% below consensus of MOP777M/day (flat YoY) and down 16% WoW; week-3 run-rate fell to MOP613M/day. JPMorgan's estimates are already 5% below FY26-27 consensus and expects material earnings downgrades, with preference for Galaxy and Wynn over Melco and SJM.

bullets.title: Wolfe DC Policy: lame-duck Congress expected to deliver less, not more, after midterms
bullets.body: Wolfe Research expects the post-midterm world to resemble the pre-midterm world, with Democratic Senate majority odds in the mid-60s to mid-70s (Wolfe takes the under on a blue tsunami). The five-week lame-duck session faces four competing priorities: election contestation, Republican reconciliation prospects, government funding, and permitting/China NDAA — but individual Republican legislators are seen as less willing to take tough votes as the trifecta ends.

bullets.title: Global inflation webcast: energy shocks pass through in 2-3 quarters; US tariff disinflation may partially offset
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's global inflation webcast flagged that energy shocks feed into producer costs within 2-3 quarters, with diesel as the broadest second-round channel. US tariff disinflation should partially offset energy-led producer-price pressure; pass-through to core inflation depends on basket weights, external price exposure, and fiscal/demand buffers. Restaurant commodity costs returned to year-over-year inflation in late October with diesel and cheese near multi-year highs.
